result:
I compared every table's "Indexes" section in `docs/db/*.md` against the actual Drizzle schema in `src/server/db/schema/*.ts`. Two discrepancies stand out:

1. **`docs/db/tables-issues.md`** — the Indexes table lists `issues_project_number_idx` as covering `org_id, number` ("enforced per organization so a number is unique across the whole tenant"). The schema (`src/server/db/schema/issues.ts:39`) actually declares it as `uniqueIndex("issues_project_number_idx").on(table.projectId, table.number)` — i.e. `project_id, number`, not `org_id, number`. (The same document's own Invariants section later correctly says "unique within `(project_id, number)`", contradicting its own Indexes table.)

2. **`docs/db/tables-webhooks-search-and-infra.md`** — the Indexes table for `search_index` lists a second index, `search_index_org_updated_idx` on `(org_id, updated_at)`, "letting the reindex job find the stalest documents first." The schema (`src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts:67-69`) only declares `index("search_index_org_kind_idx").on(table.orgId, table.subjectKind)` — there is no `search_index_org_updated_idx`, and the table doesn't even have an `updated_at` column (only `indexed_at`).

All other tables' documented indexes (organizations, users, sessions, password_reset_tokens, members, invitations, projects, project_members, comments, attachments, subscriptions, invoices, webhook_endpoints, webhook_deliveries, rate_limit_buckets, notifications, notification_preferences, activity, labels, issue_labels) match the schema exactly.

ANSWER: docs/db/tables-issues.md, docs/db/tables-webhooks-search-and-infra.md
